name: Wyoming
overview: In Wyoming, each county treasurer sells delinquent real property taxes at a tax sale; the buyer gets a certificate of purchase (a tax lien), not the property. State law lets these sales be made by lottery or by public auction to the highest bidder for cash, and the lottery-style draw is what the large counties describe. The treasurer signs and delivers a certificate of purchase to each buyer, and certificates can be assigned to someone else by endorsement. Redemption terms, interest and the waiting period before a tax deed are summarized on each county's own page below.

sales.note: Held at the Albany County Fairgrounds, east side of the Activity Building. Buyers must be present and 18 or older. Certificate of Purchase fee $20.

counties.how_to_bid: Register in person on sale day (7:45 am); the name on the registration must match the name on the payment, and each taxpayer ID gets one buyer number. Buyer numbers are drawn at random; when yours is called you may buy one property by calling its property number, or pass. Leaving the room forfeits your number. Pay in full by 5 pm on sale day. The owner may redeem in the 4 to 6 years after the sale.

counties.how_to_bid: The county sells tax liens to attending purchasers. Buyers cannot pick properties: the treasurer announces each delinquent property and draws a number, and the matching participant may buy the lien or pass. Liens must be paid when the sale ends (cash, certified funds, personal checks or credit cards, with a card fee). Buyers earn 15% per annum interest plus a 3% penalty; a tax deed may be applied for no earlier than four years after the sale.

counties.how_to_bid: You must pre-register in the Laramie County Treasurer's office (no online or day-of-sale registration). Buyers cannot pick properties: each delinquent property is announced and a number is drawn, and the matching participant may buy the lien or pass. Liens are paid in full when the sale ends. State law gives the lien buyer 15% per annum interest plus a 3% penalty; if not redeemed within four years, the buyer may obtain a tax deed. The sale notice is published in the Wyoming Tribune-Eagle.
